after 2,000 hours i feel like im ready to make an informed review. Ive been a fan of the total wars for a couple decades atp and this game combines two things i love warhammer and total war, not just combines them but combines them WELL. This game is an amazingly fun strategy game with hundred of unique units and infinite ways to play the game. I own all the dlc's to date and i have never had buyers remorse from any of them even the ones with a less than stellar rating. if your a fan of long detailed war strategy games or are just a warhammer fan you should give this game a try and if anything about the game isnt to your liking check the workshop the modding community is extensive and very active. for instance the latest patch came out 4 days ago and i play with around 30-40 QOL mods and in four days 90-95% of them were updated. This is 100% worth the money and it goes on sale every couple weeks so if your sitting on the fence wishlist it until the price drops.

This game is 2 parts, the campaign and the battles. Campaign is a 4x lite global map where you move your armies and engage in light diplomacy and the battles are RTS(rtt) scenarios where you crush the enemy army with yours, ideally.

it will be a long time before we get anything else like this game, IE specifically. The variety, the tactics, the faction differences, not to mention the passionate mod scene- one could easily dump THOUSANDS of hours into this game. I plan to.

Leaves major bugs (and easily fixed ones) unaddressed for months and only releases fixes when additional paid content is ready to launch with it. Releases DLC scaled back from previous titles with a massive price hike. When faces with backlash releases the most tone deaf response possible that doesn't address anything and contains veiled threats to stop any future support if the DLC doesn't sell.

Creative Assembly has lost touch with it's audience and eroded all good will it had with the community that plays it's game. The game itself is fun (if flawed) but I won't spend another dollar on it unless someone in CA leadership at least starts to pretend to care about the players they want to get money from sometime very soon.

Best in the trilogy. Did have a little bit of roughness on launch (some questionable design re: the pacing of the base game campaign), but now with the Immortal Empires campaign, it's the greatest fantasy Warhammer experience you'll get.

The new siege battles are pretty amazing (if long), and make defending towns a lot more viable. Plus it's just awesome to see each race's towns and cities, noting the visual differences in culture and architecture.

The new alliance system is awesome too. You get to use a limited amount of your allies' units in your armies, meaning that all sorts of mixed-race builds are now viable. Skaven gunners + Ogre Mournfang cavalry? Yes please.

Just note that you'll need Warhammer 1 and 2 to access Immortal Empires though, so keep that mind before you buy.
